transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Well, what brought me in is... I've been having some trouble with my eating lately. After my evening class, I sometimes stop for food and just end up eating a whole lot. I'll have a full fast-food meal, grab some candy from the vending machine, and then eat even more snacks once I get home. It's almost like I'm trying to make up for the whole day all at once.
When you're eating all of that food at once, do you feel like you can't control yourself or stop eating even if you want to?

Yeah, I do. It's exactly like that. Once I start on those snacks, I keep telling myself to just close the bag and go to bed. But... my hands just keep reaching for more. I really can't seem to stop until I feel embarrassed and, well, sick of myself.
After these episodes of eating a lot, do you ever try to make up for it by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or doing something else to avoid gaining weight?

Yeah, I have. Um... a few times, anyway. After those late-night eating spells, I've gone to the bathroom and made myself throw up. I just get so scared that all that food is going to show on me, so... yeah, I've done that to try and get rid of it.
Do these episodes of eating a lot usually happen when you're feeling stressed, upset, or in a bad mood?

I haven't really noticed a connection like that, to be honest. I mean, I'm not usually upset or in a particularly bad mood when it happens. Work can be a little stressful sometimes—I do bookkeeping, so the paperwork can pile up—but the eating doesn't really seem tied to that. It's more just... I get out of my evening class, I'm really hungry, and once I start eating, it just gets away from me.
Do you regularly use behaviors like vomiting, laxatives, fasting, or excessive exercise to try to prevent weight gain after eating a lot?

Yeah, I guess it has become a regular thing. For about the past three months or so, there's usually at least one night each week after my evening class where I overeat like that. And then... yeah, I make myself throw up afterward.
When you overeat like this, does it usually happen in a single, short period of time—like within a couple of hours—or does it spread out more over the evening?

It's usually all within a short period, yeah... probably just a couple of hours. Right after my evening class, I'll stop for food and end up eating a full fast-food meal. Then I'll grab some candy from the vending machine, and by the time I get home, I just keep going with even more snacks. It all happens right in a row, almost like I'm making up for the whole day all at once.
When you're eating all of that food at once, do you feel like you can't control yourself or stop eating even if you want to?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Once I start on those snacks at home, I keep telling myself to just close the bag and go to bed. I know I've had enough. But... my hands just keep reaching in for more. It's like I can't stop it, even when I really want to. I just keep going until I feel completely embarrassed and sick of myself.
When you have these episodes where you eat so much, are you actually hungry at the start, or do you keep eating even after you're full?

I'm not really sure if I'm actually hungry when it starts. I mean, I haven't eaten much all day, so maybe a little? But once I start, I definitely keep eating way past the point of being full. Even when my stomach feels tight and uncomfortable, I just keep going.
Do you usually eat alone during these episodes, or are you around other people?

I'm always alone. I make sure of it. If I stop for the fast food, I'll eat it in my car in the parking lot where no one can see me. And the rest of it... I wait until I'm home by myself. I'd be too ashamed to let anyone see me eat like that.
Do you feel guilty or ashamed after these eating episodes, and is that why you make sure to do them alone?

Yes, exactly. I feel incredibly guilty and disgusted with myself afterward. That's a big part of why I hide it. I know it's not normal to eat that much, and if anyone saw me, they'd probably think I was out of my mind. So, yeah, the shame is definitely why I make sure I'm completely alone.
How often do you feel this kind of loss of control while eating, and is it something that causes you a lot of distress in your daily life?

I'd say it happens a couple of times a week. And yes, it really does bother me. It's like... once I start on those snacks, I keep telling myself to just close the bag and go to bed. But my hands just keep reaching for more. I just can't seem to stop until I feel completely embarrassed and sick of myself. So, yeah, it causes me a lot of distress.
How often do you make yourself vomit after these episodes of eating a lot?

For about the past three months, it's usually been at least one night each week. It mostly happens on a night after my class... I'll overeat like that, and then, yeah, I make myself throw up afterward.
Do you feel a strong concern about your body shape or weight that strongly influences how you see yourself or makes these episodes feel worse?

Yes, I do. It's... well, on days when my shirt feels tight around my middle, I just feel like I've completely failed. I really try to be a careful, disciplined person, you know? And even if everything else is going well—like, even if all my bookkeeping work at the office is perfectly fine and in order—I just can't shake that feeling of failure if my clothes feel tight. It definitely dictates how I see myself and makes the whole thing feel a lot worse.
When you make yourself throw up after eating all that food, is it mainly because you're afraid of gaining weight, or is it more about feeling physically sick from eating so much?

It's definitely about the weight. I mean, feeling full is uncomfortable, sure, but... the main reason I do it is because I'm terrified of putting on pounds. If I step on the scale the next morning and it's up even just a single pound, I get this awful knot in my stomach. I just start worrying that the people in my class are going to look at me and see some sloppy old guy who just completely let himself go. So, yeah, I do it to stop the weight gain.
